# Overview

This file reads the two annotated workbooks independently, attaches **one cluster assignment per participant from the corresponding experiment × condition cluster CSV**, and conducts **separate** analyses for six groups:

1. Experiment 1 — Curvature instruction
2. Experiment 1 — No instruction
3. Experiment 2 — Curvature instruction
4. Experiment 2 — No instruction
5. Experiment 3 — Curvature instruction
6. Experiment 3 — No instruction

For Experiments 1 and 2, **human and AI coding are shown separately**. Experiment 3 currently uses **human coding only**; the AI slot is reserved for future data. The feature-mention analysis includes the coded indicators (including Size and the animal-like indicator for Experiments 2 and 3). **Priority 1–3** and **notes** are reserved for later analyses. Missing indicator codes are preserved as `NA`, not recoded as zero.

**File placement:** Put this `.Rmd`, the human Excel workbook, and (when available) the Experiments 1–2 AI workbook in `OOO_Curvature/Open_Answer_Analysis/`. Leave the experiment-specific `participant_cluster_lookup.csv` files where the main analyses exported them. This `.Rmd` accesses them at these *relative paths*:

- `../Exp1/Exp1_curvature/participant_cluster_lookup.csv`
- `../Exp1/Exp1_noInstr/participant_cluster_lookup.csv`
- `../Exp2/Exp2_curvature/participant_cluster_lookup.csv`
- `../Exp2/Exp2_noInstr/participant_cluster_lookup.csv`
- `../Exp3/Exp3_curvature/participant_cluster_lookup.csv` (if available)
- `../Exp3/Exp3_noInstr/participant_cluster_lookup.csv` (if available)

The relative paths are resolved from the `.Rmd` directory when knitting in RStudio. The human workbook is expected to have `exp1 curv`, `exp1 noInstr`, `exp2 curv`, `exp2 noInstr`, `exp3 curv`, and `exp3 noInstr` (case and spaces are normalized when matching). The AI workbook is only used for Experiments 1 and 2. If the AI workbook cannot be found, the script warns and continues with human coding only for all three experiments. Experiment 3 cluster CSVs are optional: if absent, Experiment 3 word clouds and nonclustered summaries still run, but its cluster plots are skipped.

Experiment 1 and 2 previously contained 35, 36, 36 and 36 participant records, respectively. Experiment 3 counts are computed from the workbooks at runtime. Some rows without participant IDs are continuation text, **not additional participants**.

```{r}
library(readxl)
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(knitr)

human_file <- "Curvature Open Answers.xlsx"
ai_file <- "Curvature_Open_Answers_AI.xlsx"

if (!file.exists(human_file)) {
  stop("Human Excel workbook not found: ", human_file,
       ". Put it beside this Rmd file or change human_file.")
}

# Do NOT require an AI file for Experiment 3.
# If the Exp1–2 AI workbook is unavailable, continue with human-only analyses
# rather than failing at file.exists(ai_file).
has_ai_exp12 <- file.exists(ai_file)
if (!has_ai_exp12) {
  warning("AI workbook for Experiments 1–2 not found: ", ai_file,
          ". Running human coding only. If you expect Exp1–2 AI results, ",
          "correct the ai_file path above.")
}
```

## Import all six study sheets 
```{r}
normalize_id <- function(x) {
  sub("\\.0+$", "", trimws(as.character(x)))
}

binary_code <- function(x) {
  x <- trimws(as.character(x))
  x[is.na(x) | x == ""] <- NA_character_

  if (any(!is.na(x) & !(x %in% c("0", "1")))) {
    stop("A coding column contains a value other than 0, 1, or NA.")
  }

  as.integer(x)
}


# Resolve sheet names despite changes in case/spacing.
resolve_sheet <- function(file, requested, optional = FALSE) {
  available <- readxl::excel_sheets(file)
  norm <- function(x) gsub("[^a-z0-9]", "", tolower(x))
  match <- which(norm(available) == norm(requested))
  if (length(match) == 1L) return(available[[match]])
  if (optional) {
    message("Skipping missing optional sheet '", requested, "' in ", basename(file))
    return(NA_character_)
  }
  stop("Missing Excel sheet '", requested, "' in ", basename(file),
       ". Available sheets: ", paste(available, collapse = ", "))
}

read_answers <- function(file, sheet, experiment, condition, coder, optional = FALSE) {
  sheet_found <- resolve_sheet(file, sheet, optional = optional)
  if (is.na(sheet_found)) {
    return(tibble(
      experiment = character(), condition = character(), coder = character(),
      subj_id = character(), answer = character(), smoothness = integer(),
      vertices = integer(), third_feature = integer(), intuition = integer(),
      globalness = integer(), animal_like = integer(), size = integer()
    ))
  }

  dat <- read_excel(file, sheet = sheet_found, col_types = "text")

  if (experiment %in% c("Exp 2", "Exp 3")) {

    # Experiments 2 and 3: 6 indicators (columns 3–8), plus size.
    dat <- dat[, 1:9]

    names(dat) <- c(
      "subj_id", "answer", "smoothness", "vertices",
      "third_feature", "intuition", "globalness", "animal_like", "size"
    )

  } else {

    # Exp1 has 5 indicators (columns 3–7)
    dat <- dat[, 1:8]

    names(dat) <- c(
      "subj_id", "answer", "smoothness", "vertices",
      "third_feature", "intuition", "globalness", "size"
    )

    dat$animal_like <- NA_character_
  }

  dat %>%
    filter(!is.na(subj_id), trimws(subj_id) != "") %>%
    mutate(
      subj_id = normalize_id(subj_id),
      across(c(smoothness:animal_like, size), binary_code),
      experiment = experiment,
      condition = condition,
      coder = coder,
      .before = 1
    )
}

# Human coding
human <- bind_rows(
  read_answers(human_file, "exp1 curv",
               "Exp 1", "Curvature instruction", "Human"),
  read_answers(human_file, "exp1 noInstr",
               "Exp 1", "No instruction", "Human"),
  read_answers(human_file, "exp2 curv",
               "Exp 2", "Curvature instruction", "Human"),
  read_answers(human_file, "exp2 noInstr",
               "Exp 2", "No instruction", "Human"),
  read_answers(human_file, "exp3 curv",
               "Exp 3", "Curvature instruction", "Human"),
  read_answers(human_file, "exp3 noInstr",
               "Exp 3", "No instruction", "Human")
)

# AI coding: Experiments 1 and 2 only (if their AI workbook is available).
# Experiment 3 is deliberately excluded until you have AI-coded Exp3 sheets.
ai <- if (has_ai_exp12) {
  bind_rows(
    read_answers(ai_file, "exp1 curv",
                 "Exp 1", "Curvature instruction", "AI"),
    read_answers(ai_file, "exp1 noInstr",
                 "Exp 1", "No instruction", "AI"),
    read_answers(ai_file, "exp2 curv",
                 "Exp 2", "Curvature instruction", "AI"),
    read_answers(ai_file, "exp2 noInstr",
                 "Exp 2", "No instruction", "AI")
  )
} else {
  # Same column schema as the human data, but no rows.
  human[0, ] %>% mutate(coder = character())
}

# FUTURE EXP 3 AI CODING (intentionally inactive):
# When an AI workbook with Exp3 sheets exists, add those read_answers()
# calls here and include them in ai, then update the ID coverage check below.
# read_answers(ai_file, "exp3 curv",
#              "Exp 3", "Curvature instruction", "AI")
# read_answers(ai_file, "exp3 noInstr",
#              "Exp 3", "No instruction", "AI")

answers <- bind_rows(human, ai)

# Check number of participants per group and coder
answers %>%
  count(experiment, condition, coder, name = "n_participants")
```

## Checking participant IDs
```{r}
# Check for duplicates
duplicates <- answers %>%
  count(experiment, condition, coder, subj_id) %>%
  filter(n > 1)

print(duplicates)
stopifnot(nrow(duplicates) == 0)

# Compare human vs AI participant coverage ONLY for Experiments 1 and 2.
# Exp3 has human coding only, so its missing AI IDs are intentional.
keys <- c("experiment", "condition", "subj_id")

if (has_ai_exp12) {
  human_ids <- human %>%
    filter(experiment %in% c("Exp 1", "Exp 2")) %>%
    select(all_of(keys))
  ai_ids <- ai %>% select(all_of(keys))

  only_human <- anti_join(human_ids, ai_ids, by = keys)
  only_ai <- anti_join(ai_ids, human_ids, by = keys)
  print(only_human)
  print(only_ai)
  stopifnot(nrow(only_human) == 0, nrow(only_ai) == 0)
} else {
  message("Skipping human–AI ID comparison: Exp1–2 AI workbook unavailable.")
}

```

## import cluster info
```{r}
read_clusters <- function(file, experiment, condition, optional = FALSE) {
  if (!file.exists(file)) {
    if (!optional) stop("Missing cluster CSV: ", file)
    message("Missing optional Experiment 3 cluster CSV: ", file,
            ". Skipping cluster-specific results for this group.")
    return(tibble(experiment = character(), condition = character(),
                  subj_id = character(), cluster = character()))
  }

  dat <- read_csv(
    file,
    col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
    show_col_types = FALSE
  )

  if (!all(c("subj_id", "cluster") %in% names(dat))) {
    stop("Cluster CSV needs subj_id and cluster: ", file)
  }

  dat %>%
    transmute(
      experiment = experiment,
      condition = condition,
      subj_id = normalize_id(subj_id),
      cluster = trimws(as.character(cluster))
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(subj_id), subj_id != "") %>%
    distinct()
}

cluster_lookup <- bind_rows(
  read_clusters(
    "../Exp1/Exp1_curvature/participant_cluster_lookup.csv",
    "Exp 1", "Curvature instruction"
  ),
  read_clusters(
    "../Exp1/Exp1_noInstr/participant_cluster_lookup.csv",
    "Exp 1", "No instruction"
  ),
  read_clusters(
    "../Exp2/Exp2_curvature/participant_cluster_lookup.csv",
    "Exp 2", "Curvature instruction"
  ),
  read_clusters(
    "../Exp2/Exp2_noInstr/participant_cluster_lookup.csv",
    "Exp 2", "No instruction"
  ),
  read_clusters(
    "../Exp3/Exp3_curvature/participant_cluster_lookup.csv",
    "Exp 3", "Curvature instruction", optional = TRUE
  ),
  read_clusters(
    "../Exp3/Exp3_noInstr/participant_cluster_lookup.csv",
    "Exp 3", "No instruction", optional = TRUE
  )
)

# Number of participants in each cluster
cluster_lookup %>%
  count(experiment, condition, cluster, name = "n_participants")

```
## Check and join the cluster assignments
```{r}
# Check for conflicting cluster assignments
cluster_duplicates <- cluster_lookup %>%
  count(experiment, condition, subj_id) %>%
  filter(n > 1)

print(cluster_duplicates)
stopifnot(nrow(cluster_duplicates) == 0)

# Check for missing cluster labels in the lookup
stopifnot(
  !any(is.na(cluster_lookup$cluster) | cluster_lookup$cluster == "")
)

# Identify participants without a cluster match
missing_clusters <- answers %>%
  distinct(experiment, condition, subj_id) %>%
  anti_join(cluster_lookup, by = keys)

print(missing_clusters)

# Join cluster assignments
answers_all <- answers %>%
  left_join(cluster_lookup, by = keys)

# Keep only participants with clusters for cluster-based analyses
answers_clustered <- answers_all %>%
  filter(!is.na(cluster), cluster != "")

if (nrow(missing_clusters) > 0) {
  warning(
    nrow(missing_clusters),
    " participant(s) lack cluster assignments. Verify them in the main analysis."
  )
}

# Check final numbers by cluster
answers_clustered %>%
  distinct(experiment, condition, subj_id, cluster) %>%
  count(experiment, condition, cluster, name = "n_participants")
```

## Prepare the five features and check missing coding values
```{r}
answers_long_all <- answers_all %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(
      smoothness, vertices, third_feature,
      intuition, globalness, animal_like, size
    ),
    names_to = "feature",
    values_to = "mentioned"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    feature = case_when(
      feature == "smoothness" ~ "Smoothness",
      feature == "vertices" ~ "Vertices",
      feature == "third_feature" & experiment == "Exp 1" ~ "Angle",
      feature == "third_feature" & experiment %in% c("Exp 2", "Exp 3") ~ "Range",
      feature == "intuition" ~ "Intuition",
      feature == "globalness" ~ "Globalness",
      feature == "animal_like" ~ "Animal-like",
      feature == "size" ~ "Size"
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !(experiment == "Exp 1" & feature == "Animal-like")
  )

# Check missing indicator codes
missing_codes <- answers_long_all %>%
  group_by(experiment, condition, coder, feature) %>%
  summarise(
    n_missing = sum(is.na(mentioned)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(n_missing > 0)

print(missing_codes)

# Dataset for cluster analyses
answers_long <- answers_long_all %>%
  filter(!is.na(cluster), cluster != "")
```

## Feature mention rates by cluster
```{r}
mention_rates <- answers_long %>%
  group_by(experiment, condition, coder, cluster, feature) %>%
  summarise(
    n_coded = sum(!is.na(mentioned)),
    n_mentioned = sum(mentioned == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    proportion = if_else(
      n_coded > 0,
      n_mentioned / n_coded,
      NA_real_
    ),
    percentage = 100 * proportion
  )

# 95% Wilson confidence intervals
z <- qnorm(0.975)

mention_rates <- mention_rates %>%
  mutate(
    denominator = 1 + z^2 / n_coded,
    center = (proportion + z^2 / (2 * n_coded)) / denominator,
    half_width = z * sqrt(
      proportion * (1 - proportion) / n_coded +
      z^2 / (4 * n_coded^2)
    ) / denominator,
    ci_lower = 100 * pmax(0, center - half_width),
    ci_upper = 100 * pmin(1, center + half_width)
  ) %>%
  select(-denominator, -center, -half_width)
```

```{r}
# Experiment 1, curvature instruction
mention_rates %>%
  filter(
    experiment == "Exp 1",
    condition == "Curvature instruction"
  ) %>%
  select(
    coder, cluster, feature,
    n_mentioned, n_coded, percentage
  ) %>%
  mutate(percentage = round(percentage, 1)) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  print(row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(ggh4x)

# Consistent project colors
feature_cols <- c(
  "Smoothness" = "#F8766D",
  "Vertices" = "#00BA38",
  "Angle" = "#619CFF",
  "Range" = "#619CFF",
  "Intuition" = "#A78BFA",
  "Globalness" = "#B59B73",
  "Animal-like" = "#CC79A7",
  "Size" = "#E69F00"
)

plot_open_answers <- function(exp, cond) {

  dat <- mention_rates %>%
    filter(
      experiment == exp,
      condition == cond
    )

  if (nrow(dat) == 0) {
    message("No cluster-coded results for ", exp, " / ", cond,
            "; skipping this mention-rate chart.")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }

  cluster_ns <- answers_clustered %>%
    filter(
      experiment == exp,
      condition == cond
    ) %>%
    distinct(subj_id, cluster) %>%
    count(cluster, name = "n_participants")

  # Set the correct features for each experiment
  feature_order <- if (exp == "Exp 1") {
    c("Smoothness", "Vertices", "Angle",
      "Intuition", "Globalness", "Size")
  } else {
    c("Smoothness", "Vertices", "Range",
      "Intuition", "Globalness", "Animal-like", "Size")
  }

  # Set cluster order
  clusters <- sort(unique(as.character(dat$cluster)))
  
  # Add n to cluster labels
  cluster_labels_df <- tibble(cluster = clusters) %>%
    left_join(cluster_ns, by = "cluster") %>%
    mutate(
      strip_label = paste0(cluster, " (n = ", n_participants, ")")
    )
  
  cluster_labels <- setNames(
    cluster_labels_df$strip_label,
    cluster_labels_df$cluster
  )
  
  dat <- dat %>%
    mutate(
      feature = factor(feature, levels = feature_order),
      cluster = factor(cluster, levels = clusters, labels = cluster_labels[clusters]),
      coder = factor(coder, levels = c("Human", "AI"))
    )
  
  # Colored cluster headings
  cluster_colors <- ifelse(
    grepl("smooth", clusters, ignore.case = TRUE),
    "#F8766D", "#00BA38"
  )
  
  cluster_fills <- ifelse(
    grepl("smooth", clusters, ignore.case = TRUE),
    "#FDE8E6", "#E8F7EC"
  )
  cluster_strip <- ggh4x::strip_themed(
    background_x = ggh4x::elem_list_rect(
      fill = cluster_fills,
      colour = rep("black", length(clusters)),
      linewidth = rep(0.6, length(clusters))
    ),
    text_x = ggh4x::elem_list_text(
      colour = cluster_colors,
      face = rep("bold", length(clusters)),
      size = rep(12, length(clusters))
    )
  )

  # Figure
  ggplot(
    dat,
    aes(
      x = feature,
      y = percentage,
      fill = feature
    )
  ) +

    geom_col(
      width = 0.65,
      alpha = 0.65,
      color = "black",
      linewidth = 0.4
    ) +

    geom_errorbar(
      aes(
        ymin = ci_lower,
        ymax = ci_upper
      ),
      width = 0.15,
      linewidth = 0.5,
      color = "black"
    ) +

    ggh4x::facet_grid2(
      rows = vars(coder),
      cols = vars(cluster),
      strip = cluster_strip,
      axes = "x",
      remove_labels = "x"
    ) +

    scale_fill_manual(values = feature_cols) +

    scale_y_continuous(
      breaks = seq(0, 100, 20),
      limits = c(0, 100),
      labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))
    ) +

    labs(
      x = "Feature mentioned",
      y = "Participants mentioning feature (%)",
      title = paste(exp, "—", cond)
    ) +

    theme_classic(base_size = 14) +

    theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      axis.text.x = element_text(
        angle = 35,
        hjust = 1,
        size = 10
      ),
      panel.spacing = grid::unit(12, "pt"),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_line(
        color = "grey92",
        linewidth = 0.3
      ),
      plot.title = element_text(
        size = 16,
        face = "bold"
      )
    )
}
```

# Word Frequencies and Word Clouds

The following nine word clouds use the revised term lists. Size-related terms have been
removed from the submitted lists; other counts are preserved exactly as provided.
Word sizes represent raw frequencies; percentages are calculated relative to the revised
list for each feature. The plots above (feature mention rates) now also support Experiment 3 when cluster CSVs exist.

```{r word-frequency-tables}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggwordcloud)
library(tibble)

# Convert named frequency vectors to tidy, percentage-adjusted tables
make_word_freq <- function(counts) {
  tibble(term = names(counts), frequency = as.integer(unname(counts))) %>%
    arrange(desc(frequency), term) %>%
    mutate(percentage = 100 * frequency / sum(frequency))
}

# EXP1 SMOOTHNESS — 84 total mentions
word_freq <- make_word_freq(c(
  "sharpness" = 19,
  "curved" = 13,
  "pointiness" = 7,
  "smoothness" = 7,
  "roundness" = 6,
  "straight" = 6,
  "softness" = 4,
  "corner" = 2,
  "curvature" = 2,
  "hard" = 2,
  "angle" = 1,
  "brash" = 1,
  "continuous" = 1,
  "curve" = 1,
  "curviness" = 1,
  "curvy" = 1,
  "harshness" = 1,
  "jagged" = 1,
  "peaks" = 1,
  "pointy" = 1,
  "rigidity" = 1,
  "spikes" = 1,
  "tips" = 1,
  "triangle-like" = 1,
  "wave" = 1,
  "zigzag" = 1
))

# EXP1 VERTICES — 47 total mentions

  "number of bumps" = 13,
  "number of curves" = 10,
  "number of peaks" = 6,

  "number of angles" = 2,

  "number of humps" = 1,

  "number of vertices" = 1
))
```

## Word clouds (Experiments 1–3)

```{r plot-nine-wordclouds, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
# One plotting function keeps formatting consistent across all nine clouds.
dir.create(
  "open_answer_outputs/figures",
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)

plot_wordcloud <- function(dat, low, high, filename, shorten_number_of = FALSE) {
  dat <- dat %>%
    mutate(label = if (shorten_number_of) sub("^number of ", "", term) else term)

  set.seed(123)
  p <- ggplot(dat, aes(label = label, size = frequency, color = frequency)) +
    ggwordcloud::geom_text_wordcloud_area(rm_outside = TRUE) +
    scale_size_area(max_size = 60) +
    scale_color_gradient(low = low, high = high) +
    theme_void() +
    theme(legend.position = "none")

  print(p)
  ggsave(
    filename = file.path("open_answer_outputs", "figures", filename),
    plot = p,
    width = 10,
    height = 6,
    dpi = 300
  )
  invisible(p)
}

# Exp 1 — consistent experiment-prefixed output names
p_wordcloud <- plot_wordcloud(
  word_freq, "#FBC8C4", "#D94B42", "exp1_smoothness_wordcloud.png"
)
p_vertices_wordcloud <- plot_wordcloud(
  vertices_word_freq, "#A5E8B7", "#008A29", "exp1_vertices_wordcloud.png",
  shorten_number_of = TRUE
)
p_angle_wordcloud <- plot_wordcloud(
  angle_word_freq, "#BFD6FF", "#326BC9", "exp1_angle_wordcloud.png"
)
```
